headline: Comparative genomics links protein complex, secretome, and prokaryotic genome evolution
label: Comparative Genome And Proteome Analysis
summary: Recent preprints and a published archaeal survey apply orthology, structural, and pangenome comparisons across eukaryotes, fungi, and prokaryotes.
synthesis: The common thread is comparative inference over sequence-defined units, with evidence drawn from orthogroups, structural folds, and genome-scale pangenomes. A preprint mapping experimentally verified protein complex components onto orthogroups across 31 eukaryotes identifies 184 universal orthogroups and quantifies within-complex duplications. A Zymoseptoria passerinii secretome analysis finds 72 structural clusters in which effector folds are conserved, with diversification occurring through surface changes. On the prokaryotic side, a complete gap-free Ralstonia F1C1 genome and a 142-genome pangenome of the Ralstonia solanacearum species complex identify 651 recurrent integration spots linked to accessory-genome function. A survey of 7,747 archaeal genomes reports fewer defense systems than in Bacteria and identifies archaea-enriched candidate systems.
